newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Steady on stable regional demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Steady on stable regional demand.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel markets were steady Thursday on crude gains and regional demand, traders said.

The draw in middle-distillate stocks in Singapore for the second week running which traders attributed to the recent cuts in refinery runs also boosted sentiment. Shell has so far restored runs to full capacity while Esso has not yet done so.
Stocks for the week ended February 26 fell 518,000 barrels to 7.27 million barrels.

Indonesia has bought 3.5 million barrels of gas oil on a cost-and-freight basis for March deliveries which traders said covered its requirements for that month. The price was 20-30 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes.
Indonesia has also covered its jet fuel requirements for March after buying about 1.3 million barrels.
Traders said Indonesia has bought more gas oil and jet fuel for March because of the shutdowns at the Dumai and Balongan refineries.

In Singapore two gas oil cargoes were traded. A US trader sold a cargo at $25.15 a barrel for March 14-18 lifting fob to a Singapore trader, while another Singapore trader sold to a Thai trader at $25.00 a barrel for March 25-29 lifting fob.
Another 30,000-tonne cargo was heard traded at a 25-cent-per-barrel premium to Singapore quotes for early April lifting fob, which reflected the rising premium level.
China was said to have bought a 30,000 tonne cargo for mid-March delivery at $197 a tonne, c-and-f northern China. This was below the last cargo sold to China at $202, c-and-f southern China.
Traders are also closely watching India's second gas oil tender for April delivery closes on Wednesday. India bought 570,000 tonnes in its first tender.
Jet fuel was offered at $27.00 a barrel, up from the last deal at $26.80.
Unlike the steady physical market, swaps gas oil for March was quoted 20 cents lower than Wednesday.
